MSFT.rationale: Microsoft presents a solid fundamental case with strong revenue growth (+18.3% YoY in Q3 FY2026), excellent margins (gross margin 68.8%, operating margin 46.3%, net margin 35.7%), and robust cash generation (operating cash flow $46.7B in the quarter). The AI business is scaling rapidly at a $37B annual run rate (+123% YoY), Azure continues growing at 40%, and the balance sheet is fortress-quality with $78.3B cash against only $40.3B debt. However, several factors temper the score: (1) the stock has declined ~31% from its 52-week high of $555 to $379, partly reflecting legitimate concerns about massive capex ($190B planned for calendar 2026) compressing free cash flow and returns on capital; (2) multiple class-action lawsuits alleging misleading Copilot statements create legal overhang; (3) the collapsed Oracle cloud deal and intensifying regulatory scrutiny on AI/cloud practices add uncertainty; (4) QoQ EPS declined 17.2% from Q2 to Q3, suggesting some earnings volatility. On valuation, the current P/E of 27x is near the low end of its 25.4-42.8x range over the past year, and P/B of 7.8x is at the bottom of its 7.3-12.6x range, making it cheap relative to its own history. The next earnings report (July 28, 2026) could serve as a near-term catalyst if Azure growth reaccelerates or capex guidance moderates. Net-net: excellent franchise at a reasonable valuation, but capex intensity, legal risks, and execution uncertainty on AI monetization prevent a higher score.
